newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill dips to 10.159 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill dips to 10.159 pct.

text.p: The Philippine benchmark 91-day treasury bill rate fell to an average of 10.159 percent from 10.564 percent in the previous week, the Bureau of Treasury said on Monday.
"I expect the average rate to drop, but not this low," a dealer in a foreign bank told Reuters.
The dealer said the average of the 91-day T-bill is the lowest since October 1995 when the rate hit 10.08 percent.
"Perhaps some banks submitted a low bid to ensure that they get some T-bills in today's auction," the trader said.
Traders said the market is now awash with cash due to a dearth of investment instruments.

They also expected the Central Bank to cut anew its overnight rates on Tuesday following a slash on March 4 in its overnight borrowing to 10.4375 percent from 10.5 and its lending rate to 12.9375 percent from 13.0.

Central Bank treasurer Sergio Edeza said he does not see any speculation in the foreign exchange market even if the peso only now has a 2.5 percent premium over the U.S. dollar. Inflows coming in the country are looking at the prospective growth of the economy, he told Reuters after the T-bill auction on Monday.
The 182-day T-bill rate dropped to an average 10.4 percent from 10.725 in the previous week while the 364-day T-bill fell to 10.871 percent from 11.212 percent.
The auction had tenders worth 27.77 billion pesos, of which 4.5 billion pesos were awarded.
Traders said the decline in the interest rates was also encouraged by the Central Bank when it stopped offering the 89-day T-bill at a rate of 10.5 percent earlier on Monday.
One trader said the drop in the rates was also in line with the fall of the year-on-year February inflation rate to a decade low of 4.4 percent.
